question.problem:
Negate the following statement: 

$\,$ At least one existential statement is not true.
question.worked_solution:
Let $E$ be the set of all existential statements. The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ There exists $S\in E$ such that $S$ is not true.

Introducing the existential quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∃S\in E,\,S\text{ is not true}.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∃S\in E,\,S\text{ is not true}) & ≡∀S\in E,\,¬(S\text{ is not true}) \\  & ≡∀S\in E,\,S\text{ is true}\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ For all $S\in E,$ $S$ is true.

or simply

$\,$ Every existential statement is true.

choices.value: Every existential statement is not true.
